content:
alex: heads-up — during the last deploy we saw a spike of cold-prefix misses when pods came up after the autoscaler scaled. p99 generation latency +120ms for a 30s window.

mira: ugh. which model and route?

simon: perf-bot: uploaded a quick hit-rate dump -> s3://perf/2419998999/prefix_hitrate_top_routes.csv :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex: model: text-slim-v2, route: /chat/assist. traffic pattern: many short prompts with identical prefixes (UI flows).

dante: quick note — kernel selection looked fine. profiler shows KV cache lookups as the main cold path (misses + disk fallback) not batch scheduling.

mira: ok. so we should avoid on-demand population when pods start. propose a deploy-time preloader job that seeds the in-memory KV for the top prefixes for that model+route.

grace: agreed. two constraints: 1) job must be region-aware (seed local nodes), 2) should respect rate limits so it doesn't create thundering requests to downstream connectors.

alex: draft idea: after canary -> primary switch completes, run a per-cluster job that posts synthetic inference requests for the top-N prefixes. keep them short and cheap (max 16 tokens).

mira: note about keying: we should align preloader keyhashing with runtime key derivation. we had a bug earlier where seeder used "prefix+route" but runtime normalized to "prefix|model" so misses happened. double-check canonicalizer.

simon: here's a minimal job payload we used for local tests:

```json
{
  "endpoint": "/v1/generate",
  "model": "text-slim-v2",
  "prompt": "Summarize: <TOP_PREFIX>",
  "max_tokens": 8,
  "metadata": {"preload": true}
}
```

alex: also add a small sleep/jitter between requests to avoid bursting the batcher. something like 50-200ms per prefix.

perf-bot: small analysis: seeding top-200 prefixes reduced miss-rate from 18% -> 3% in the canary test. overall cost 0.6% extra tokens for the cluster window.

dante: kernel selection note — for a lot of these short tokens we should force the quantized fast-path to avoid kernel dispatch overhead, otherwise preloads still cost too much CPU. i'll put a flag in the preloader to set runtime.preferred_kernel=fast_q8.

mira: good. what about autoscale events (not deploys)? when new nodes spin up mid-day we still get misses. we need a lightweight continuous scheduled job that runs every 5m and only seeds prefixes with recent traffic delta.

grace: maybe a hybrid: deploy-time full seed (top-N), and a micro-prober that reacts to scale-out events using the same prefix delta. micro-prober should only target the new node IPs.

alex: infra-bot: can we capture scale-out hooks? we can subscribe to cluster-autoscaler events and trigger the micro-prober job with node list.

infra-bot: yes — we have an autoscale webhook. will add a small lambda that calls /ops/preload with node filter.

mira: metrics to watch: prefix_hit_rate, kv_miss_rate, p50/p95 generator latency, token-cost delta per hour. add an eval prompt set to ensure quality unchanged.

perf-bot: regression test plan: run A/B for one region: A = existing behavior, B = deploy+micro-prober. capture 24h heatmap and cost. expected p95 drop ~50-80ms on the targeted route.

dante: one more caution: prefix entropy. seeding top-200 is great for stable UI prefixes but not helpful for high-entropy user input. we should calculate per-prefix entropy and only seed prefixes with entropy < 4 bits.

alex: action items:
- dante: add kernel flag and canonicalizer check (owner).
- mir a: write micro-prober blueprint + rate limits.
- simon: add preload job k8s template and upload to ops repo.
- grace: wire autoscale webhook -> infra-lambda.
- perf-bot: run canary A/B and post results.

mira: i'll take coordination, will post RFC tomorrow. :thumbsup:

grace: 👍

simon: sounds good, i'll start the job template.

alex: thanks — keeping this lightweight should avoid cost surprises. we can iterate on top-N and entropy thresholds after initial canary.

perf-bot: scheduled canary kickoff at 2419999100.
